newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gurkhas in cash quarrel with Britain.
newsitem.headline: Gurkhas in cash quarrel with Britain.

text.p: Gurkha representatives on Thursday accused London of consistently short-changing the Nepali soldiers, who fought alongside British troops in both world wars, and threatened to sue for compensation.

"This is a plea about justice," Eric Urbani, a representative of the Gurkha Army Ex-Servicemen Organisation, told a news conference in Hong Kong, where up to 15,000 former Gurkhas still live after serving with the British colony's garrison.
The last Gurkha units in Hong Kong were disbanded this year and London hands back the territory to China on July 1 after more than 150 years of British rule.
"Given the handover...really this is our last chance to say something and take action before (Hong Kong) is no longer part of the British empire," Urbani said.
The group accused Britain of discrimination against Gurkhas in pay, pension, benefits and promotions. It also said a trust fund set up by the Gurkhas had disappeared.
It said pay for a Gurkha serviceman or ex-serviceman was only 10 to 15 percent that of his British counterpart.
"The discrimination by the British government had a real and tragic impact on the life of Gurkha veterans and their families," Urbani said.
"Many Gurkha soldiers have given life and limb to Britain in Malaysia, in Indonesia and the Falklands. They have returned to a life of grinding poverty in the hills and mountains of the Himalayas."
The group blamed Britain for not accounting for the disappearance of an 80 million pound (US$134 million) trust fund raised by Gurkhas between 1968 and 1971 and managed by the British army.
"To this day, we don't know what happened to this fund. It has disappeared," Urbani said. Yubaraj Sangroula, a lawyer for the ex-Gurkhas, said the group was considering taking the case to court.
British Defence Ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.
